open_points.subject: answer_request
open_points.text: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
open_points.other_text: The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
open_points.question: For an oversized body or failed token check, must the body remain unread, or must it be read to preserve a string or integer id in the refusal response?

open_points.subject: answer_request
open_points.text: the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
open_points.other_text: A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
open_points.question: Must every JSON-RPC request name and authorize a catalogue operation, or do initialize, ping and tools/list bypass those catalogue-operation checks?

open_points.subject: answer_request
open_points.text: Before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1).
open_points.other_text: Text an agent supplies — purposes, implementation code, names, JSON texts — is data: it is never evaluated, imported, compiled, formatted or interpreted in the kernel process; no answer and no refusal carries a token, a service credential, a host path or a stack trace, an internal error included (A16 rules 5 and 7).
open_points.question: Must supplied JSON texts be interpreted as JSON to canonicalize them, or must they never be interpreted in the kernel process?

open_points.subject: run_start_sequence
open_points.text: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason;
open_points.other_text: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason;
open_points.question: When an exception's original reason does not name the failing step, must it be propagated unchanged or modified/wrapped so that its reason names the step?
